scope: Engine source, public C++ runtime API, CLI discovery/profiling, regression fixtures and canonical engine documentation only.

platform.android: Source clock policy preserved; no new native build/device qualification.
platform.ios: Source clock policy preserved; no new native build/simulator/device qualification.
platform.macos: Prior elapsed clock policy retained; no native build/qualification.

coverage: Interpreted/native runaway hooks, pcall/xpcall and nested module/state callbacks
Windows sleep/CPU clocks plus private deterministic failure/fallback policy fixtures
VM memory errors, bounded UTF-8 diagnostics and source locations
Passive failed-world observation, save/scene refusal and completed-save reconstruction
Migration metadata, large input decoding and failed input decoding preserving memory classification/running world
Optional binding profiling including on_load/on_recover inheritance
Callback preview original-failure records and distinct recovery errors
Assets/audio, scene-local catalogs, content cooking and game workflow tooling
Graphics capture, live controls, source reload, failure pause, player isolation and receipt concurrency

checks.command: Package script PowerShell AST parse and scoped git diff --check

observed_clock_fixture.note: One standalone observation, not a precision guarantee.

observed_native_fixture.note: Deliberately expensive bounded native work demonstrates that synchronous C++ cannot be preempted at 50 ms.

benchmark.interpretation: Synthetic before/after medians differ by about 1-3%; timing noise prevents claiming a speedup. Large fixture write conversion/copy/serialization dominates. Profiling is optional and adds clock reads; coarse CPU counters may report zero or a 15.625 ms increment for short bindings. JSON write algorithms/limits are unchanged.

qualification_limits: The original frontend incident cause remains unknown; fixing the wall-clock false-positive mechanism does not prove every incident had that cause.
Windows GetThreadTimes accounting is coarse. 1 ms query cadence is not 1 ms CPU precision or a hard real-time deadline.
No new device, remote-machine, custom frontend or Core qualification.
Historical distributions and frontend binaries were not regenerated. A custom host must adopt the public API and handle exceptions/recovery itself.
Native diagnostic JSON allocation and persistence are best effort under actual process-wide memory/I/O failure; the 16 MiB cap applies to the Lua VM.
No human gameplay acceptance is inferred from engine fixtures.
